Genetic architectures

Source: R/architecture.R
architectures.Rd

An architecture maps a genome to genotypic values. Genomes are matrices of allelic effect vectors (traits x alleles); alleles \(2l - 1\) and \(2l\) belong to locus \(l\), and the effect of a locus is the sum of its two alleles (\(Y_l\)). Effects are measured from the reference genotype, where all effects are zero.

Usage

additive(loci, traits)

binary_b(loci, traits, init_b = 0.25, init_y = c("normal", "mutations"))

contribution_matrix(
  traits,
  genes = traits,
  init_weights = rep(1, genes),
  init_contributions = diag(1, traits, genes)
)

multilinear(loci, traits, epsilon)

Arguments

loci

number of diploid loci.

traits

number of traits.

init_b

probability that an entry of B is 1 in a new population (0.25 in the C code, which starts from random mutations of an empty B).

init_y

how allelic effects y of a new population are drawn, with the model's init_sd: "normal", Normal(0, init_sd) for every allele; "mutations", as in the C code, 2 x loci mutations of Normal(0, init_sd) added to alleles chosen at random in each genome.

genes

number of weight genes.

init_weights

starting values of the weight genes (one per gene).

init_contributions

starting contribution matrix (traits x genes); by default ones on the diagonal (gene j affects trait j only, the identity when genes == traits).

epsilon

epistasis coefficients: a traits x traits x traits array shared by all pairs of loci (symmetric in its last two indices; see random_epsilon()), or a traits x traits x traits x loci x loci array with a different tensor for every pair of loci, as in Jones, Burger & Arnold (2014) (see pairwise_epsilon()). For the pairwise form, epsilon[k, a, b, i, j] multiplies Y_i[a] Y_j[b] in trait k, and only entries with i < j are used.

Value

An evomod_architecture object.

Details

  • additive(): \(x = \sum_l Y_l\).

  • binary_b(): the binary ontogenetic matrix model of Melo & Marroig (2015). Each allele has a scalar effect \(y\) and a column of a binary matrix \(B\) saying which traits it affects; \(x = B y\). Use with binary_b_mutation(). Genomes have traits + 1 rows: \(y\), then \(B\).

  • contribution_matrix(): the model of do O & Whitlock (2023). genes weight genes \(a_j\) and a traits x genes matrix of contribution genes \(c_{ij}\), each its own locus with a scalar value (the two alleles of a locus are summed); \(x_i = \sum_j c_{ij} a_j\). Pleiotropy (\(C\)) evolves continuously and can be negative, and the map is bilinear (epistasis between weight and contribution genes). Loci 1..genes are the weight genes; locus genes + (j - 1) * traits + i is \(c_{ij}\). Use with contribution_mutation(). New populations start with every individual at init_weights and init_contributions (each allele half of the locus value), plus Normal(0, init_sd) noise on every allele.

  • multilinear() with a pairwise epsilon (pairwise_epsilon()): a different tensor for every pair of loci (Jones, Burger & Arnold 2014), \(x = S + \sum_{i<j} \varepsilon_{ij}(Y_i, Y_j)\).

  • multilinear(): pairwise multilinear epistasis (Hansen & Wagner 2001), \(x = S + \sum_{i<j} \varepsilon(Y_i, Y_j)\), with \(S = \sum_l Y_l\) and \(\varepsilon(a, b)_k = \sum_{l,m} \varepsilon_{klm} a_l b_m\). The same tensor is used for every pair of loci and must be symmetric in its last two indices.

Examples

additive(loci = 50, traits = 2)
#> <evomod architecture> additive - 50 loci, 2 traits
binary_b(loci = 50, traits = 4)
#> <evomod architecture> binary_b - 50 loci, 4 traits
contribution_matrix(traits = 4)
#> <evomod architecture> contribution_matrix - 20 loci, 4 traits
multilinear(loci = 50, traits = 2, epsilon = random_epsilon(2, sd = 0.05))
#> <evomod architecture> multilinear - 50 loci, 2 traits
